site.description: Local-first tennis tools from AceCrush: AceCrush Craft for grip size, racket profiles and stringing data on Android, syncing through your own Supabase account with no central AceCrush server, plus Swing Analysis for automatic swing segmentation on the desktop.

brandHero.headline:
Tennis tech that
runs on your device.
brandHero.subtext: AceCrush makes small, focused tools for tennis enthusiasts and players. Your measurements stay on your phone. Your records sync through your own Supabase account, so they follow you across devices.
brandHero.craftCardBody: Measure your grip size from a palm photo, keep a profile for every racket, log each restring with expiry reminders, and convert tension across DT, RT, lbs and kg. iOS is in TestFlight.
brandHero.swingCardBody: Drop in a match video and get every swing cut into its own clip, each labelled with ready, windup, contact and follow-through phases plus exact timecodes.

intro.headline:
Perfect Photo,
Perfect Grip
intro.subtext: On-device AI measures hand size via an A4 reference, recommends your optimal grip, and tracks your next string job.

howItWorks.heading: From photo to recommendation in under 30 seconds.
howItWorks.step1Body: Lay an A4 sheet flat on the table with your palm resting on it.
howItWorks.step2Body: Line the edges of the A4 sheet up with the green frame on screen, keep your palm open, fingers and heel fully in frame.
howItWorks.step3Body: AI returns the recommended size and adjacent sizes. You can fine-tune manually.

features.heading: What it does for you.
features.subheading: Six tools. One download. Works fully offline.
features.item1Body: Two ways, one result. AI mode runs on-device MediaPipe inference from a top-down palm photo on an A4 reference and maps to Yonex, Wilson and Head-Prince-Babolat sizing. Manual mode skips the camera and computes from palm length and ring finger length, including a wrap-driven size shift. Switch at any time, both flows share the same recommended-size output.
features.item2Body: Log multiple rackets with specs and parameters, all in one place.
features.item3Body: Record string type, stringing date and tension for each restring, set an expiry reminder, and get notified before and on the due date.
features.item4Body: Switch between DT and RT tension readings at a glance, so the number on the stringing machine matches what your racket spec sheet asks for.
features.item5Body: Sketch serves, returns and patterns on a tennis court canvas. Save tactic boards alongside a match so the next time you face the same opponent you can replay what worked.
features.item6Body: All records sync through your own Supabase project: grip measurements, racket profiles, restring logs, tactic boards and photos. Only you can see them. The local SQLite stays the source of truth on the device so the app keeps working offline.

privacyStrip.heading: Your photos sync with your account.
privacyStrip.body: AI measurement runs on-device for the inference. Both the photo and the result are saved to your Supabase account, the photo in a private Storage bucket, so they follow you across devices once you explicitly push sync from one device and pull sync on the others. Local deletes do not propagate on their own.

download.androidBody: Primary platform today. Minimum Android 7.0 (API 24), target API 34, about {fileSize}. No root and no Google Play Services required.
download.androidNote: Android blocks unknown sources on first install. Open Settings, Apps, Special app access, Install unknown apps, allow this source, then tap the APK again.
download.iosBody: iOS is in TestFlight beta. The build targets iOS 15 and up, feature-complete against the Android release, but it is rough around the edges, expect the occasional crash, missing polish, and breaking changes between builds.
download.iosNote: Tap to open TestFlight on your iPhone and accept the invite. You'll need the Apple ID signed into your device to install the build.

faq.heading: AceCrush Craft Related
faq.q1: How do I get the most out of AI measurement, and is it accurate?
faq.a1: Lay the A4 sheet flat on the table, place your palm on it, and line the four edges of the sheet tightly against the green frame on screen, with no gap and no overhang. Fingers and heel must stay fully inside the frame. Shoot straight down. When those conditions hold, the recommended size is reliable within one adjacent size, with a confidence hint shown on the result card. We do not claim millimeter precision and we do not fabricate percentages.
faq.q2: Do I have to use A4 paper, and what about the green frame?
faq.a2: A4 is the recommended reference because its 210 by 297 mm dimensions are baked into the pixel-to-millimetre conversion. Other sheets or known-size objects work too if you tell the app their real dimensions. The green frame exists for one reason: pixel calibration depends on the A4 edges being aligned to it, so gaps or overhangs skew every downstream measurement.
faq.q3: What if my photo is taken at an angle, or my hand is off the sheet?
faq.a3: Confidence drops to medium or low and the result can drift by one or two grip sizes. Re-take the photo from straight above, palm flat on the A4, with the sheet edges tight against the green frame. The manual path inside Grip size measurement stays available regardless: type palm length and ring finger length and skip the camera entirely.
faq.q4: How does data sync work across devices?
faq.a4: Sync is explicit, not automatic. On the device where you made changes, open Settings and tap Push sync to upload. On every other signed-in device, open Settings and tap Pull sync to download. Local deletes do not propagate on their own. The full step-by-step walkthrough, including conflict rules when two devices edited the same record offline, lives in the cloud sync guide.

intro.headline: Every swing, cut and timecoded.
intro.subtext: Feed in a match video. The two-pass pipeline tracks a single right-wrist signal, cuts each swing into its own clip, and labels ready, windup, contact and follow-through with exact timecodes.

features.heading: Built for frame-level review.
features.subheading: Three things it does that scrubbing a timeline cannot.
features.item1Body: The v2.1 pipeline reads one right-wrist signal to find swing boundaries, then refines them offline. Every segment carries ready, windup, contact and follow-through phases with timecodes.
features.item2Body: Segments appear while pass 1 is still running, so you can start reviewing before the full video finishes processing.
features.item3Body: Want to see the body lines on each clip? Two passes to choose from. The **fast pass** paints the skeleton while it cuts — quick and good enough for a first review. The **polish pass** re-renders each clip afterward with a steadier person box and a smoother skeleton — slower, but the kind of cut you'd hand to a student. Both bake straight into the export, no post-processing needed.

download.desktopBody: Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. A Python backend plus an Electron GUI, with a CLI for terminal use. The models ship inside the repo, so clone and run works offline.
download.releasesNote: GitHub will redirect you to the current latest release.

faq.heading: Swing Analysis Related
faq.q1: Does my video get uploaded, and which models actually run on it?
faq.a1: Nothing leaves your machine. The local service binds to 127.0.0.1 only, so the video never reaches a server. Two model families matter here: the wrist tracker that drives swing segmentation (MediaPipe pose, by default, with a MoveNet fallback) and the optional overlay models that paint the skeleton and person box (RTMDet plus RTMPose). The first family is always on, because segmentation depends on it. The overlay family is opt-in and re-renders the clip after segmentation, never influencing where the cuts land.
faq.q2: Do different model choices change the segmentation result?
faq.a2: Yes, but only the segmentation models can. Switching the wrist tracker from MediaPipe pose to MoveNet can shift swing boundaries by a few frames and occasionally split or merge adjacent swings, so the choice matters for fast, jerky matches. Switching the overlay models only changes how each already-cut clip is painted, never where the cuts are.
faq.q3: Are the clip cuts and the overlay effects one step or two?
faq.a3: They are two separate steps. Pass 1 cuts every swing into its own clip using the wrist tracker only, with no overlay drawn. The optional polish pass runs afterwards on the saved clips, re-detecting the person and re-drawing the skeleton and box. Either pass can be skipped, and skipping the polish pass leaves you with cuts but no overlays. Clips are saved to disk between the two passes, so you can also re-run just the polish pass later.
faq.q4: Do I need a GPU, and can I drive the pipeline without the desktop GUI?
faq.a4: No GPU is required, the whole pipeline runs on CPU. The overlay models are the heaviest step and the main reason a GPU helps when you have one, so turn them off for the fastest first pass on weaker machines. The CLI drives the exact same pipeline, and the local REST plus WebSocket service on port 8321 is open to any front end you want to build on top.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.section1Body: Your records in AceCrush Craft (grip size measurements, racket profiles, restring logs, and the photos you take for measurement) live in your own Supabase account. Only you can see them, and AceCrush does not run any extra backend on top of it: the Supabase project IS where your data is stored. Your device keeps a local copy too, so the app keeps working offline.
privacy.section2Title: Sync across every device you sign in to
privacy.section2Body: Sign in with the same Supabase account on another device (Android today, iOS in TestFlight beta, desktop later) and your records show up there too. Sign out on a device and its local copy gets cleared the next time it syncs.
privacy.section3Camera: Camera (android.permission.CAMERA): used only on the AI measurement screen. Revoke in system settings to disable.
privacy.section3Notification: Notifications (android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS): used only for restring expiry reminders. Disable in system settings.
privacy.section4Body: When you take a measurement photo, the app processes it on-device with MediaPipe HandLandmarker. If your hardware cannot keep up, the photo is sent once to our server-side OpenCV plus MediaPipe pipeline. Either way, the result and the photo itself are then saved to your Supabase Storage bucket, scoped per user. We do not retain the photo on the server after it lands in your bucket.
privacy.section5Body: Your login and your data are handled by Supabase (supabase.com). We do not run any other backend on top of it. The app also uses these open source libraries locally: Flutter, drift, flutter_local_notifications, url_launcher, opencv_dart, MediaPipe Tasks Vision. None of them send data anywhere.
privacy.section6Body: Policy updates ship with new app releases and are reflected both in the in-app Settings - Privacy policy screen and on this page. Questions: acecrushdev@gmail.com.
